source.title: A Scaling Law for Syn2real Transfer: How Much Is Your Pre-training Effective?
source.authors: Hiroaki Mikami; K. Fukumizu; Shogo Murai; Shuji Suzuki; Yuta Kikuchi; Taiji Suzuki; S. Maeda; Kohei Hayashi

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present; the text identifies it as a preprint.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling behavior in synthetic-to-real vision transfer and refines its scope by reporting sensitivity of the fitted pre-training rate to data complexity and instability in jointly fitting curve parameters.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own downstream test-error scaling results for vision transfer, including model-size and data-complexity sweeps. It does not test language-model cross-entropy, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or downstream performance as a function of pre-training loss. Other studies' scaling results cited in Related Work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law-plus-constant laws to downstream vision error as synthetic pre-training data, fine-tuning data and ResNet size vary. This is a new setting (syn2real vision transfer) with its own results on V5, V6 and V7. It does not challenge or restate a version, so T3 fits better than the reader's T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that syn2real fine-tuning error follows test error ≈ Dn^-α + C, which generalises to a multiplicative law in pre-training and fine-tuning size and agrees with their NTK-based bound. The law holds across tasks, model sizes and data complexities. They also conclude that bigger models and closing the domain gap reduce the transfer gap C, and that α slows with data complexity. They list as limitations: ResNets only, million-scale data, few vision tasks; extension to language is left as future work.
record.recipe_differences: Studies synthetic-image transfer in vision, measuring downstream task error as pre-training and fine-tuning data sizes vary; it does not use the original language-model cross-entropy scaling method.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted pre-training rate varies with synthetic-image complexity. Estimated transfer gap generally falls as appearance, light, and background complexity increase, but not for object texture. Joint fitting of D and α was unstable; the authors fixed D = 0.48 and estimated α and C.

fits_no_version.finding: The transfer-gap plateau C falls with added appearance, light and background diversity, but rises when object textures are added (attributed to texture shortcut learning).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The irreducible error floor of transfer scaling depends on pre-training data diversity and domain gap, not only on scale.

fits_no_version.finding: A theoretical NTK/ASGD bound gives a multiplicative form (c + A n^-α) s^-β for fine-tuning error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theory predicts a multiplicative pre-training × fine-tuning power-law form for transfer error.

record.problems: The study is limited to ResNet architectures, vision tasks, and data scales up to million-scale. Several plotted results lack textually reported individual values. The authors report instability between D and α and fix D = 0.48, which may bias α estimates; the normal→semseg α estimate is highly unstable, with standard deviation larger than 1. The theoretical analysis uses assumptions that may not match the experiments, including averaged SGD and identical task types.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small-run fits to much larger runs. The million-scale runs are shown following the law, but no out-of-sample prediction is reported.
Compute-optimal allocation of parameters and data.
Effect of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Generative image/video models, repeated data, language transfer and non-ResNet architectures. Only syn2real ResNet transfer up to 1.28M images is tested.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss, and language tasks.
Parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, and disagreement between published laws.

missing.what: D and α are nearly degenerate in the least-squares fit: curves with D=0.5, α=0.4 and D=1, α=0.5 are almost indistinguishable at large n. D was fixed at 0.48 by an iterated median.
Per-task-combination estimates of α (roughly 0.2–0.8) and C with standard errors, showing the exponent varies by pre-training/fine-tuning task pair.
In linearized plots, some points for mulclass→semseg and normal→semseg become negative after subtracting C, indicating poorer fit there.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The law is power-law-plus-constant with only α and C fitted per setting (D fixed), on 7 pre-training sizes, so a good fit is partly by construction. The record lists peer review as ECML/PKDD, but the text says preprint; this cannot be verified from the text. The rows' figure-only states for R1–R12 are appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and its dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs' language-model loss from fits to smaller language-model runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as compute changes.
Effect of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests synthetic-to-real vision transfer with synthetic pre-training data; does not test language, image/video generative models, repeated data, or the other listed training regimes.
Tests downstream vision error against pre-training data size, not downstream performance against pre-training loss; does not test language-model tasks.
Reports data-complexity dependence and fitting instability, but does not compare published language-model laws, parameter-counting conventions, or training schedules.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.stage_stated: synthetic multi-label classification pre-training, then ImageNet fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Jointly vary pre-training and fine-tuning data sizes and fit the full scaling law.
rows.measure: ImageNet test error as a function of pre-training size n and fine-tuning size s; fit of Equation (2).
rows.value: The empirical errors are described as explained remarkably well by the four-parameter law; α = 0.544, β = 0.322, γ = 0.478, and δ = 41.8.
rows.note: Fine-tuning data sizes ranged from 2% to 64% of ImageNet; E was assumed to be 0.

rows.subject: Two-layer neural network with M hidden units
rows.size_stated: Width M; sufficiently large for the stated arbitrarily small approximation term
rows.operation_detail: Derive a generalization-error upper bound for transfer using averaged SGD under NTK assumptions.

conditions.value: Regression with square loss; shared input distribution; fine-tuning target φ0 + φ1

rows.measure: Upper bound on fine-tuning generalization error.
rows.value: E_x L(n,s) ≤ A1(cM + A0 n^−α)s^−β + εM; exponents depend on φ0, φ1, input distribution, and fine-tuning learning rate.
rows.uncertainty: High-probability bound; no numerical probability specified in the informal statement.
rows.note: This is a theoretical bound under stated assumptions, not an empirical measurement of language-model loss.
rows.check: This is a theoretical upper bound under NTK and averaged-SGD assumptions, not an empirical measurement. It should not carry an 'observed' state.

relationships.condition: Syn2real ResNet transfer: fine-tuning error vs pre-training size, fine-tuning size, and C vs model size
relationships.reason: Power law plus constant fits most task combinations (R13) and holds to 1.28M images (R20, R21). The joint four-parameter law fits ImageNet fine-tuning (R30). Fine-tuning-size scaling is power-law (R15), and C scales roughly as a power of model size (R18, R19).
relationships.display_finding: Power laws plus constants fit most tasks through 1.28M images; a joint four-parameter law fit ImageNet fine-tuning, and approximate power laws described error versus fine-tuning size and the constant versus model size.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Syn2real ResNet transfer: fine-tuning error vs pre-training size, fine-tuning size, and C vs model size
source_check.reason: R13, R15, R18–R21 and R30 support power-law scaling with an additive transfer gap in the tested vision-transfer regimes.

relationships.condition: Cross-task fits with small fine-tuning sets; normal→semseg
relationships.reason: The pre-training exponent is unidentifiable for normal→semseg (α SD >1, Appendix C.1; R11). Fits required fixing D across settings, and pre-training gains plateau at a large C (R14).
relationships.display_finding: The normal-to-semantic-segmentation pretraining exponent had standard deviation above one; fits required fixing D across settings, and pretraining gains plateaued at large C.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Cross-task fits with small fine-tuning sets; normal→semseg
source_check.reason: R11 establishes uncertainty in the normal→semseg exponent, not failure of the scaling form. Fixing D addresses parameter degeneracy; the plateau in R14 is explicitly part of the fitted law. These facts do not establish a V5 scope failure.

relationships.condition: Downstream COCO/ADE20K/ImageNet error vs synthetic pre-training size and model size
relationships.reason: Downstream error falls predictably along the fitted law across task combinations and million-scale data (R13, R20, R21, R30). Larger ResNets give lower error (R16, R17).
relationships.display_finding: Downstream error followed the fitted law across task combinations and million-scale synthetic datasets, while larger ResNets achieved lower error.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Downstream COCO/ADE20K/ImageNet error vs synthetic pre-training size and model size
source_check.reason: Section 4.2 reports accurate downstream-error fits in most cases; Section 4.3 reports lower errors for larger models; R20, R21 and R30 extend the fitted relationships across larger data sizes.

relationships.condition: Large pre-training data or large fine-tuning data
relationships.reason: Pre-training benefit diminishes at large n, and the plateau dominates (R14). The authors argue the relative gain from pre-training vanishes when fine-tuning data is large (Section 3.3).
relationships.display_finding: Pretraining benefits plateau at large data scales, with fitted saturating and multiplicative laws predicting vanishing relative gains as fine-tuning data grows.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Large pre-training data or large fine-tuning data
source_check.reason: R14 and Section 3.3 describe diminishing gains predicted by the fitted saturating and multiplicative laws. V6 does not require unbounded gains; no breakdown of downstream predictability is demonstrated in this condition group.

relationships.reason: The fitted exponent α changes with data complexity (R22–R25). The text also reports strong D–α degeneracy requiring D fixed at 0.48 (Appendix D; not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: The fitted exponent α changes with rendering complexity, while strong D–α degeneracy requires fixing D at 0.48.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Sections 4.5 and 5.1 report complexity-dependent exponents. Section 4.1 and Appendix D report D–α degeneracy and fixing D at 0.48; Section 4.5 acknowledges possible resulting bias in α.
